title: Runtime hot-reload and schema evolution notes
content:
Context and goal:

This is a messy personal scratchpad about ideas for supporting safe hot-reload of runtime configuration + graceful schema evolution for the serving runtime. Objective: allow ops and control-plane to push changes (routing, quant profiles, batcher tiers, fallback maps, kernel hints) without restarts, while guaranteeing no silent behavior regressions and clear rollback semantics.

Constraints and invariants (opinionated):
- Changes must be transactional at a per-tenant or per-pool granularity (not necessarily whole process).
- New config keys can be added; old keys may be deprecated but still accepted for N releases.
- Any change that affects live inference path must go through a validation + dry-run check.
- Metric continuity: any hot-reload should emit a lineage signal tying pre/post metrics together (config_id, activate_time).
- Prefer feature-flags + staged rollout to immediate global flips.

Primary failure modes to protect against:
- Schema mismatch causes runtime panic on handler lookup (null refs).
- Silent change of semantics (e.g., caching TTL changed units: ms->s).
- Partial application: some workers apply config, others don't -> inconsistent routing.
- Backpressure/queueing blowup due to new batching thresholds.

Core proposal sketches:
1) Config manifest and versioning
- manifest metadata: {config_id, schema_version, created_by, description, compatibility: {min_runtime_version, compatible_keys:[...] } }
- each logical config piece (batcher, router, kernel-hints, quant-profile) must declare a small interface: "apply(config_blob) -> apply_report" + "validate(config_blob) -> validation_report".
- runtime stores both active_config_id and staged_config_id; activate call is an atomic switch point coordinated by leader (see coordinator below).

2) Schema evolution model (a tiny compatibility DSL)
- SchemaVersion integer + diffs. Ops: ADD_KEY (safe), REMOVE_KEY (breaking), RENAMED_KEY (breaking unless alias declared), CHANGE_TYPE (maybe-breaking unless compatible coercion defined).
- Each schema diff includes migration hints and optional server-side migration code (JS/wasm sandbox?). For simple coercions we'd use built-in transforms (int->float, seconds->ms with unit annotation).

3) Activation workflow (staged rollout)
- submit config -> validation phase (all affected components validate w/ dry-run)
- stage to subset: control-plane picks shard set (eg 5% of pool) -> send staged_config_id with TTL and rollout metadata
- monitor signals: errors, latencies, request-level correctness checks (unit tests + smoke prompts), cost regressions
- on success, promote to active with atomic leader-coordinated commit that flips active_config_id in metadata service (consistent store)
- if leader commit fails, fallback to previous active_config_id and emit rollback telemetry

4) Coordinator design
- Use existing control-plane leader in the cluster (or elect via etcd/raft) to orchestrate activation.
- Steps (rough):
  a) push manifest and blobs to object store (immutable)
  b) write "staged: <config_id>" to cluster metadata with target_shards list and epoch
  c) workers watch metadata and pull staged config; apply in "staged" mode and report apply_report
  d) coordinator waits for quorum of healthy reports or timeout then flips active_config_id
  e) workers observe active_config_id flip and switch live routing tables atomically
- Timeouts and partial failures: workers include "apply_liveness" TTL; coordinator can mark worker_unhealthy and exclude from promotion set

5) API shapes (rough)
- POST /internal/configs -> {manifest, blobs[]} returns config_id
- POST /internal/configs/{id}/validate -> triggers cluster-wide dry-run validation, returns validation_id
- POST /internal/configs/{id}/stage -> {target: "shards=10%"} returns rollout_id
- POST /internal/rollouts/{rollout_id}/promote -> atomic commit
- POST /internal/rollouts/{rollout_id}/abort -> rollback
- GET /internal/configs/{id}/status -> validation + apply reports
- Webhook callbacks: on-promotion, on-abort with metrics snapshot link

6) Worker apply model (safe switching)
- Each component exposes a small lifecycle: validate -> prepare -> quiesce -> swap -> post-check.
  - validate: stateless sanity checks
  - prepare: allocate ephemeral resources (e.g., compile kernel changes into ephemeral plan)
  - quiesce: drain in-flight requests relevant to the component (short window)
  - swap: atomically swap pointer(s) (C++ atomic pointer / go: value swap) to new plan
  - post-check: run synthetic smoke requests (can be configured per-config) -> report
- If any step fails, worker returns error and attempts local rollback to previously held plan

7) Telemetry and SLO/KSIs to emit
- config.apply_attempt (config_id, worker_id, step, result, duration, error_code)
- config.promotion (rollout_id, success:Boolean, duration, changed_keys)
- config.rollback (reason, impacted_requests_count)
- metric continuity tags: attach config_id + config_epoch on all inference spans for N hours after rollout

8) Testing and lab plan
- Local fuzzer that mutates manifests (add/rename/remove keys) and checks validators; run in CI for PRs touching schema
- Blue/green simulation harness in staging: deploy fake traffic profiles and ensure no request-level regressions
- Canary gating: build threshold checks in the promotion step (e.g., no CPU spike > 15%, no error-rate increase > 0.1%)

Open questions / TODOs (random personal notes):
- What is the minimum atomicity we need? Per-tenant, per-pool, per-process? I think per-pool is an OK default but some Dedicated customers will want per-tenant isolation.
- Quiesce strategy needs careful thought for streaming sessions (KV cache mutation in-flight). Maybe do logical fence per-session id range? Hard.
- How expensive is prepare step for kernel-recompiles? Need offline cost model; maybe only allow warmup/lib load in prepare, compile lazily on first use with a compatibility marker to reject until compiled.
- Sandbox for migration transforms: do we want JS/wasm to express migrations? Potential attack surface but very flexible. Alternatively provide a small builtin transform language (enough for unit conversions and renames)
- How do we test semantic changes to quant profiles? Must run a small accuracy eval on a curated prompt set as part of staged rollout. Can be slow -> use sample queries + offline eval - but costy.

Notes on compatibility helpers (brainstorm):
- "alias" map: allow old keys to map to new keys at runtime. Control-plane can inject aliases per manifest.
- "coercion hints": declarative transforms (units, scale, parse pattern) and a small library of safe coercions.
- "compat_mode": for N releases, runtime can accept both old and new keys; runtime resolves precedence (new overrides old).
